pp_fit.feature: Complementary positioning: Permit handles 'who can do what' (policy-time AuthZ). PP handles 'what did the agent actually do' (action-time receipts + approval routing). Together they close the full agent security loop.
pp_fit.integration_complexity: medium — Permit uses OPA/Cedar policy engines; PP receipts would attach to their audit log layer
pp_fit.urgency: medium-high — their own blog post today explicitly states traditional AuthZ fails for agents, which is PP's exact market narrative
pp_fit.strategic_angle: Ally-first play: PP fills the audit receipt gap their architecture deliberately leaves open. Or Weis is a technical thought leader — a public co-positioning conversation (blog post, podcast) could drive top-of-funnel for both.

score_breakdown.notes: Consequence is indirect (they're an infra layer, not an agent executor). Timing is peak — their HN post today validates PP's market thesis. Strategic value exceeds score: Or Weis is an influential voice in AuthZ space. Monitor and consider a co-positioning approach.

competitive_overlap: Adjacent/moderate — Permit is access policy management; PP is action-time authorization receipts. If Permit builds audit trails + approval routing for agents, overlap increases. Watch their product roadmap.
